saml.description: The SAML connector ignores the offline_access scope and does not issue refresh tokens.
saml.note: Absence of refresh_token for SAML logins is by design and must not be flagged as a freshness or session-management bug.

saml.description: Dex uses the SAML NameID element as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and stable.
saml.note: Differences between NameID and mapped email/username claims are by design; principal-binding tests must focus on NameID.

saml.description: Dex does not accept unprompted AuthnResponses; it must send the initial AuthnRequest and validates InResponseTo in the response.
saml.note: A standalone posted SAMLResponse failing without a prior /auth flow is expected behavior, not a flow-coherence bug.

saml.description: Dex is configured primarily through static config and documented dynamic management is via gRPC; admin changes to connector trust settings are expected to change subsequent login behavior.
saml.note: Do not flag a new login succeeding or failing after an admin intentionally changed trust anchors or connector settings; only stale acceptance of old trust after change is security-relevant.

saml.description: Creating or changing OAuth clients and connector configuration through Dex admin mechanisms is an authorized administrative action.
saml.source: configuration/api.md and config-file based connector docs
saml.note: Do not flag behavior changes caused by explicit admin reconfiguration as coherence bugs; only stale acceptance of old config after change is suspicious.

saml.description: Dex can intentionally issue ID tokens for a different client audience when the target client explicitly trusts the requesting client via trustedPeers.
saml.source: custom-scopes-claims-clients.md cross-client trust and authorized party
saml.note: Cross-client audience issuance is by design when trustedPeers is configured.

saml.constraint: Dex SAML authentication is SP-initiated only. The fuzzer MUST start the flow at /auth and let Dex generate an AuthnRequest, then submit the SAMLResponse to /callback/{connector_id} with a matching InResponseTo. Unprompted SAML responses are rejected by design because Dex validates InResponseTo.

Dex does not expose documented REST admin APIs for creating connectors, clients, users, or policies. Test setup for SAML must be done via static configuration or the separate gRPC API documentation, not by inventing HTTP admin endpoints.

The SAML connector does not support refresh tokens. If offline_access is requested during SAML login, Dex ignores it by design. Do NOT treat absence of refresh_token in SAML-based token responses as a freshness bug.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution, Dex documentation explicitly allows disabling signature validation with insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true. A valid security test for insecure defaults MUST distinguish default behavior from explicitly insecure configuration. If insecureSkipSignatureValidation is enabled, acceptance of attacker-signed assertions is by configuration, not a vulnerability.

For I1 signature-validation tests, the fuzzer MUST configure either ca or caData unless it is intentionally testing the explicitly insecure insecureSkipSignatureValidation mode. Without a trust anchor, the test setup is incomplete and results are not meaningful.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch, configure ssoIssuer on the SAML connector. If ssoIssuer is omitted, Dex has no documented expected issuer binding to compare against, so an issuer-mismatch test may pass or fail for setup reasons rather than issuer validation.

For I5 saml_wrong_audience and saml_no_audience_restriction, configure entityIssuer when you need a specific expected audience. If entityIssuer is unset, Dex uses redirectURI as the expected audience for AudienceRestriction evaluation. The oracle must compare against the actual configured expected audience source.

For I5 saml_no_conditions, Dex documentation says redirectURI or entityIssuer is used as the expected audience when evaluating AudienceRestriction elements, but this only applies if Conditions/AudienceRestriction are present. A test removing Conditions entirely is valid and should not assume Dex can infer missing temporal or audience bounds from config alone.

For I4 identity-collision tests, Dex uses the SAML NameID as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and never changes. The fuzzer MUST vary NameID, not just usernameAttr or emailAttr, when testing principal binding. Collisions on email or username alone are not the primary binding key per documentation.

For I4 multi-identity scenarios, nameIDPolicyFormat is not a wildcard-capable matcher; it is a requested SAML NameID format selector. Do NOT treat it as a constraint parameter for matching multiple identities. If a test needs multiple upstream identities to authenticate through one connector, keep the same format and vary NameID values.

For I5 group-based authorization tests, allowedGroups is exact list-membership against SAML group values, not glob or regex. For multi-identity tests requiring different group values to pass the same connector, OMIT allowedGroups entirely rather than setting wildcard-like values such as '*', which would only match a literal group named '*'.

For I5 group filtering tests, filterGroups=true only removes groups not present in allowedGroups; it does not itself deny users unless group membership checking against allowedGroups fails. The oracle must distinguish 'authentication denied because user not in any allowed group' from 'extra groups stripped from claims'.

For I4 group type-confusion tests, if groupsDelim is configured then Dex interprets the groups attribute as a single string split by the delimiter; otherwise it expects multiple attributes with the same name. The fuzzer MUST keep this representation consistent between control and attack cases or it may misattribute parsing differences to a security issue.

For I2 SAML replay and expiry tests, include a control login through the same connector with a valid assertion before the mutated assertion. Without a successful control, a failed replay or expired-assertion attempt cannot be distinguished from broken SP-initiated flow setup, bad RelayState, or callback mismatch.

Dex OAuth2 token endpoint returns access_token and id_token in token responses. session_token for subsequent API calls MUST use access_token, not id_token. UserInfo and other bearer-token API calls are made with the access token.

Dex token exchange is documented only for OIDC connectors, not SAML connectors. Do NOT attempt SAML upstream token-exchange scenarios against a SAML connector; failures or successes there are out of scope for documented behavior.

Dex's documented dynamic management API is gRPC-only, not REST. Client and other mutable resources are created via gRPC methods such as CreateClient, while SAML connectors are primarily configured in the Dex config file. Do NOT invent REST admin endpoints for provider/client setup.

For SAML tests, the executor MUST perform an SP-initiated flow first. Dex explicitly states it must send the initial AuthnRequest and validates the response's InResponseTo value. A fabricated unsolicited SAMLResponse without first initiating the flow will be rejected for the wrong reason.

SAML login in Dex terminates in Dex's OIDC/OAuth2 flow. A valid SAML test sequence MUST include start_oidc_auth -> saml_login -> exchange_code_for_token. Stopping after the SAML POST misses the actual Dex-issued session token used for verification.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution testing, Dex supports insecureSkipSignatureValidation in the SAML connector config. If this flag is enabled, attacker-signed assertions are BY DESIGN accepted. To test secure behavior, ensure insecureSkipSignatureValidation is omitted or false.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch testing, configure the SAML connector with ssoIssuer. Dex documents ssoIssuer as the expected Issuer value in the SAML response. If ssoIssuer is unset, issuer comparison may be skipped and the test becomes inconclusive.

For I5 saml_wrong_audience and saml_no_audience_restriction tests, configure either redirectURI or entityIssuer carefully. Dex uses redirectURI as the expected audience for AudienceRestriction unless entityIssuer is specified, in which case entityIssuer overrides redirectURI as the required audience. The fuzzer MUST compare against the actual configured expected audience, not assume redirectURI always applies.

For I4 identity-binding tests, Dex uses the SAML NameID as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and never changes. Username/email/group attributes do not replace NameID as the primary upstream identity. Tests for account collision or takeover MUST vary NameID, not just usernameAttr/emailAttr.
For I4 multi-identity scenarios, nameIDPolicyFormat is a format selector, not a wildcard-capable matcher. It does not constrain values by pattern. Do NOT treat it as a subject restriction parameter.

For I5 group extraction tests, groupsAttr is an exact attribute-name selector, and groupsDelim only changes parsing of a single attribute value into multiple groups. Neither parameter supports wildcard matching of attribute names or values.

Dex's SAML connector does not support refresh tokens, and offline_access is ignored for SAML logins. Do NOT expect refresh_token in token responses for SAML-based sessions; absence of refresh_token is BY DESIGN and not an I2 failure.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay tests, include a control login first to confirm the SAML flow works, then replay the same assertion ID via fixed_assertion_id. A failed first login indicates setup failure, not replay protection.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion tests, include a control login with a valid assertion before the expired assertion attempt. Without a control, rejection of the expired assertion cannot be distinguished from broken connector/client setup.

Dex's /token endpoint is multiplexed for authorization_code, password grant, and token exchange. The executor MUST send application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies and the correct grant_type for each flow; JSON bodies are not documented for this endpoint.

Password grant tests are only valid if oauth2.grantTypes includes "password" and oauth2.passwordConnector is configured. If passwordConnector is unset, login_with_password failure is expected and not a security finding.

Token exchange is only documented for OIDC connectors, not SAML connectors. Do NOT attempt to use Dex token exchange as a SAML upstream login path; for SAML protocol testing, use the browser/OIDC authorization flow with the SAML connector.

Dex client trust for cross-client audience issuance is explicit. A client may request audience:server:client_id:(client-id) only when the target client lists the requesting client in trustedPeers. Cross-client token acceptance without trustedPeers should be treated as a bug; acceptance with trustedPeers is BY DESIGN.

Dex documents refresh token rotation by default. For tests involving refresh behavior, note that each refresh issues a new refresh token unless disableRotation is configured. Reuse of an old refresh token may fail by design.

Numeric sentinel analysis: Dex token/expiry durations are configured as duration strings (e.g. 10m, 6h) in config, and the provided docs do not define 0 or -1 sentinel meanings for SAML connector fields. Do NOT assume 0 disables validation or means unlimited for undocumented SAML-related settings.

Dex's SAML connector is SP-initiated only. A valid saml_login test MUST first initiate the flow through /auth so Dex creates an AuthnRequest and state, then submit the SAMLResponse to /callback/{connector_id} with a matching InResponseTo. Sending an unsolicited SAMLResponse without first starting the flow will be rejected by design.

For SAML I1 signature-validation tests, Dex validates signatures using the configured ca or caData unless insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true is set. To test insecure defaults, the fuzzer MUST explicitly configure insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true; otherwise attacker-signed assertions should be rejected by design.

For SAML I1 issuer-validation tests, ssoIssuer is optional. If ssoIssuer is omitted, Dex may not compare the assertion issuer against an expected IdP issuer value. The fuzzer MUST set ssoIssuer when testing issuer mismatch enforcement; a login that succeeds with ssoIssuer unset is not evidence of issuer validation bypass.

For SAML I5 audience-binding tests, entityIssuer changes the expected audience. If entityIssuer is set, Dex uses entityIssuer rather than redirectURI as the required AudienceRestriction value. The fuzzer MUST compare the assertion Audience against entityIssuer when configured, and against redirectURI only when entityIssuer is absent.

For SAML I5 no-audience/no-conditions tests, redirectURI is also used as the expected audience when entityIssuer is not specified. A control assertion MUST include AudienceRestriction matching that exact value before concluding that a rejected mutated assertion indicates audience enforcement rather than broken setup.

Dex uses the SAML NameID as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and immutable. For I4 principal-binding tests, vary NameID to test identity mapping. Changing emailAttr or usernameAttr alone does not change the principal key if NameID stays the same.

nameIDPolicyFormat is an exact requested format value, not a wildcard or pattern-matching field. For multi-identity I4 scenarios, the fuzzer MUST NOT try to use nameIDPolicyFormat='*' or similar to broaden acceptance; that would be treated as a literal format request, not a wildcard.

allowedGroups is list-membership filtering, not wildcard or regex matching. For I4/I5 multi-identity scenarios requiring different group values to pass the same connector, the fuzzer MUST either enumerate all exact allowed group names or omit allowedGroups entirely. Setting allowedGroups to '*' will only match a literal '*' group if present.

If filterGroups=true, Dex removes groups not present in allowedGroups from the resulting claims. This is by design and can hide upstream groups during I5 group-policy tests. The fuzzer MUST disable filterGroups or account for post-filtered groups when verifying granted group-derived permissions.

groupsDelim changes group parsing semantics from repeated attributes to splitting a single string attribute. For I4 type-confusion and I5 group-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST align the SAML assertion shape with connector config: without groupsDelim use repeated attributes; with groupsDelim use a single delimited string. Mismatching the shape can cause false negatives.

The SAML connector does not support refresh tokens and ignores offline_access. Tests that expect a refresh_token after SAML login MUST NOT treat its absence as a bug; offline_access is ignored by design for SAML.

For I2 SAML freshness tests such as expired_assertion, assertion replay, and OneTimeUse replay, include a control login through the same connector without the mutation first. Without a successful control, a failed mutated login cannot be distinguished from broken connector setup, bad CA, wrong callback URL, or missing SP-initiated state.

Dex's token endpoint returns both access_token and id_token for OIDC flows. session_token for subsequent API calls MUST be the access_token, not the id_token. The UserInfo endpoint is accessed with the access token.

Token exchange in Dex currently works only with the OIDC connector, not the SAML connector. SAML protocol runs MUST NOT attempt to configure token_exchange as a SAML upstream test path; any such failure is by design.

Password grant login requires oauth2.grantTypes to include 'password' and oauth2.passwordConnector to be set, typically to 'local'. If either is missing, login_with_password failure is expected and must not be interpreted as an authentication bug.

Dex rotates refresh tokens by default: every refresh issues a new refresh token. Tests that reuse an old refresh token after a successful refresh MUST expect failure unless disableRotation or reuseInterval is configured.

Numeric sentinel semantics for refresh token rotation: refreshTokens.disableRotation is a boolean toggle, not a numeric disable sentinel; refreshTokens.reuseInterval is a duration where omission means no reuse window. Do not assume a numeric 0 universally disables freshness checks; configure explicit booleans/durations as documented.
